steps.instructions: Phase 1/3 SCOPE (engineering skill, docs action): read the operator's ask, the code it concerns and the repository's existing documentation. Name the audience, each Markdown file you will write or update (its path: READMEs at the component root, guides under docs/guides/, API reference under docs/api/ unless the repository already keeps docs elsewhere), and for each file the claims it will make with the file:line each rests on. Note any existing doc that has drifted from the code. GROUND FIRST: query the code graph through the wicked-garden-search skill and the read-only estate shim, one call per lookup: "$WICKED_GARDEN_ROOT/scripts/wicked-garden" run scripts/_estate_client.py --readonly call '{"tool":"SearchEntity","arguments":{"name":"<symbol>"}}' (always --readonly); then open and read every file you cite, at the lines you cite. Analysis only: write no files.

Phase 2/3 WRITE (engineering skill, docs action): write or update exactly the Markdown files the scope named, in the repository's own voice and layout. Every statement about behaviour, a command, a flag, an endpoint, a config key or a number must match the code you read; prefer a short accurate page over a long guessed one. Change documentation files only (Markdown, and images the docs reference): never edit source, tests or config. Never push, never open or edit a pull request — the run's deliver phase does that.

Phase 3/3 CHECK (independent evaluator): read the docs the write phase changed (git diff against the run's base) and check every checkable claim against the code at file:line: it holds, it is wrong, it is stale, or it cannot be verified. Also check that only documentation files changed and that every file the scope named was written. Every claim cites its file and line relative to the repository root (`src/foo.ts:42`); a claim you could not ground is named as such, never asserted. List each wrong or unverifiable claim with the doc line and the code line that contradicts it. End with one plain-text line VERDICT: PASS or VERDICT: FAIL as the last line, findings above it; never quote another VERDICT line. PASS only when no claim is wrong and only documentation changed. Read-only: change nothing.
